about: Quentin Brogdon is a Fellow of the invitation-only American College of Trial Lawyers (Chair, Texas State Committee 2026-2027), the International Academy of Trial Lawyers, and the International Society of Barristers. He is also a member of the American Board of Trial Advocates.

He is listed in The Best Lawyers in America (Lawyer of the Year, Plaintiffs Personal Injury, Dallas and Fort Worth, 2023), and he is board certified in personal injury trial law and in civil trial advocacy. He has been a Texas Monthly Super Lawyer every year since its inception in Texas, and he has been selected as the Top Super Lawyer in Texas and one of the Top 3 Super Lawyers in Texas. L awdragon Magazine selected him as one of "500 Leading Plaintiffs Lawyers in America," and one of "500 Leading Consumer Lawyers in America." The National Trial Lawyers selected him as a Top 100 Texas Trial Lawyer, and D Magazine selected him as a "Best Lawyer in Dallas." The Dallas Bar Association Tort & Insurance Practice Section named him a "Trial Legend" in 2026.

He served as President of the Texas Trial Lawyers Association, President of the Dallas Chapter of the American Board of Trial Advocates (ABOTA), President of the Dallas Trial Lawyers Association, President of the Association of Plaintiff Interstate Trucking Lawyers of America, and Chair of the Texas State Committee of the American College of Trial Lawyers. He served on two State Bar of Texas Pattern Jury Charge Committees, and he has authored over 100 published articles on personal injury trial law topics.

The State Bar of Texas awarded him the Standing Ovation Award and the Gene Cavin Award for Excellence in Continuing Legal Education, the Texas Bar Foundation awarded him the Dan Rugeley Price Award for "commitment to clients and the profession." The Association of Plaintiff Interstate Trucking Lawyers of America awarded him the Thurgood Marshall Fighting for Justice Award for "tenacious effort against overwhelming odds in achieving success in the fight for justice," and the Texas Trial Lawyers Association awarded him the Don Bowen Distinguished Service Award for "meaningful and dedicated service to TTLA that has advanced the organization, its mission, and the civil practice of law."

He received his B.A. degree from Rice University, and his J.D. and M.B.A. degrees from the University of Houston, where he was an associate editor of the Houston Law Review . He is AV-Rated Preeminent by Martindale-Hubbell.
